sentences.text: Abrictosaurus was a bipedal creature that likely ate plants or mixed plant and animal matter, standing as one of the earliest members of the heterodontosaurid family.
This dinosaur is famous for having large, tusk-like teeth in both its upper and lower jaws, while the front of its mouth lacked teeth entirely in favor of a hard beak.
The upper tusk measured 10.5 millimeters in height, whereas the matching lower tooth grew to 17 millimeters.
Despite its modest build, the animal weighed under 45 kilograms.
Fossils of only two individuals have ever been discovered.
Richard Thulborn first described the holotype specimen in 1974, originally giving it the name Lycorhinus consors.
The name Abrictosaurus, which translates to 'wakeful lizard', was chosen to reflect Hopson's disagreement with Thulborn's theory that these dinosaurs aestivated.
Its forelimbs were smaller and less powerful than those of Heterodontosaurus, possessing one fewer phalanx bone in the fourth and fifth digits.
The animal belongs to the ornithischian dinosaur clade and is classified within the family Heterodontosauridae.
It further belongs to the subfamily Heterodontosaurinae.
The presence of caniniforms in the second specimen supports the classification of Abrictosaurus consors as a valid species.
The time range for Abrictosaurus is estimated from 201.4 to 192.9 million years ago.
The fossils date to the Hettangian and Sinemurian stages of the Early Jurassic, approximately 200 to 190 million years ago.
The habitat consisted of sand dunes and seasonal floodplains within a semiarid environment with sporadic rainfall.
Thulborn continued to classify Lycorhinus angustidens, Heterodontosaurus tucki, and Abrictosaurus consors as species within the genus Lycorhinus.

Researchers suggested that the lack of tusks in one specimen indicated it was female, or possibly a female of a different species. It is debated whether the lack of tusks represents sexual dimorphism or is instead a juvenile trait, as the specimen may be a juvenile.
